newsitem.title: SPAIN: BASKETBALL-GARCIA HOPES TO TURN AROUND NIGHTMARE SEASON.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-GARCIA HOPES TO TURN AROUND NIGHTMARE SEASON.

text.p: Coach Aito Garcia hopes to turn around Barcelona's worst basketball season in years in the EuroLeague game at Bayer Leverkusen this Thursday.

Runners-up in last season's competition, Barcelona must win the Bayer game to have any chance of going into the second round of the complicated two-tiered league system as one of the top three sides from their group.
Garcia has been forced to make changes after seeing his side founder to fifth in their group of six with just three wins in eight games in a slump that has led for calls for his resignation.
His first move was to release newly-signed Russian forward Andrei Fetissov,
Garcia had criticised Fetissov for not concentrating enough in the disastrous 81-67 Spanish league defeat at Xacobeo Orense, a side that had never beaten Barcelona.
Fetissov was also felt to be too lightweight near the basket and has been replaced by beefy American Jerrod Mustaf.
The former University of Maryland forward shone with 22 points in 33 minutes on court in his debut game in the Spanish league as Barcelona beat fellow European championship hopefuls, Estudiantes.
"Mustaf proves Aito right," read a headline in the sports daily Marca.
But despite the comprehensive 97-79 victory, Barcelona fans were quick to jeer Garcia.
"The first year they asked for my head, and the second, and the third..," commented Garcia, who has blamed the crowd for not getting behind the team enough.
But Garcia was full of praise for his new signing "Mustaf gives us greater balance," he said.

Unfortunately for Garcia, Mustaf will not be able to play in Europe until the competition enters its second phase from January 9, when the bottom three teams in each group of six will face the top three from another group.
The signs are that Barcelona will be among those bottom three, and will have to beat stronger sides to progress further.

Mustaf -- who has a track record as a difficult player -- has a further five domestic games to prove himself before then. But Barcelona are taking no chances and are looking at several other Americans in case he fails to come up with the goods.
It is ironic that Barcelona should be struggling to find foreign players, as many Spanish coaches face a weekly dilemma as to which foreigner to drop for European action.
Whereas Spain's ACB league allows the use of three non-European Union players -- predominantly Americans and East Europeans -- European championship rules permit only two.
But this season Barcelona took the unusual decision to play with just two foreigners so as to field the same starting team in every game.

One of those foreigners, Arturas Karnishovas, continues to be the most important figure in the Barcelona team, but is looking tired after spending the summer with the Lithuanian team at the Atlanta Olympics.
Commentators point out that Karnishovas spent the summer of 1995 preparing for the Euro-basket competition in Greece, and as a result has only had two weeks holiday in as many years.
Ramon Rivas has been hit by injuries and has also lost his form, something that former Barcelona centre Ferran Martinez blames on Garcia.

"In Barcelona you have to train even when your defences are down," said Martinez, who joined Panathinaikos shortly after the Greek side had beaten Barcelona in the controversial European championship final in Paris.
Barcelona were subsequently awarded 'moral compensation' by basketball authorities because of timekeeping and refereeing errors in the final minute of the game.
But Martinez is confident that his old side will recover.
"The situation at Barcelona is very serious, but I'm sure that they will get out of it," he said.
And the new championship format means that Garcia will get a second chance at winning Barcelona's first European Cup, a trophy that arch-rivals Real Madrid have won eight times.
